blocks.text: Lots and land in Burnaby Hospital

items.t: Lot character: typical lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only lot-size figures a source states for this area are the R1 SSMUH thresholds themselves: 280 m² and 281 m².

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice — the established streets sit inside that municipal system on the City's wording. Servicing for any single parcel is confirmed with the City; no well/septic position is asserted.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in this sub-area is confirmed; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission and is not verified for individual lots. No ALR percentage split is stated.

Market context, labelled correctly: Burnaby IS a SnapStats-covered community — Detached versus "Condos & Townhomes" combined only. SnapStats has NO land category, and no detached figure is a land figure. September 2026 context only: Burnaby Hospital sub-area detached inventory 13 / solds 1 (8% ratio) and "Condos & Townhomes" 10 / 0; Burnaby community detached median $1,825,000 and attached median $686,000. Sub-area medians are not verified (community level only).

No bare-land strata plan in the Burnaby Hospital sub-area was verified: The verified set is empty. If a bare-land strata lot is ever marketed here, treat it as what it is in BC: strata tenure — the buyer owns a strata lot, pays strata fees, is bound by the bylaws, and diligence runs through the Form B.

Burnaby Hospital redevelopment — 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health / Province of BC): Phase 1 delivered a new six-storey health care pavilion with 83 beds, mostly single-patient rooms, plus an expanded support facilities building with a new energy centre; renovations to existing buildings continue. On September 21, 2026 the Province announced a renewed plan: $210 million for an improved and expanded emergency department and surgical unit going ahead immediately, with expanded cancer care and a new acute-care tower to follow, building on the pavilion's March 2026 opening. This is a public institutional campus, not a land offering — its land relevance is construction activity on Kincaid Street for years and long-term employment demand beside the house lots, both of which a lot buyer should price with eyes open.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Burnaby Hospital

items.t: Burnaby Hospital is a City of Burnaby sub-area in central Burnaby — the residential streets around Burnaby Hospital, south of Canada Way and west of Deer Lake, with the hospital campus at 3935 Kincaid St (Fraser Health). "Burnaby Hospital" is the GVR board sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby; it is named for the hospital, not for a City neighbourhood plan. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; exact MLS boundary streets are not verified.
Nearby areas: Sperling-Duthie and Deer Lake to the east, Burnaby Lake to the north-east across Canada Way, Cascade Heights to the south, Forest Glen and Metrotown to the west and south-west.

Main roads: Canada Way runs east–west at the north edge; Kincaid Street serves the hospital campus; Deer Lake Parkway and Sperling Avenue link east to Deer Lake and City Hall at 4949 Canada Way. There is no SkyTrain station inside the sub-area; buses operate on Kincaid Street at the campus, and the nearest Millennium Line station is Sperling–Burnaby Lake, north-east across the Deer Lake / Burnaby Lake side — walking distance for a specific address: Not verified.

Civic and park anchors: Deer Lake Park, 6450 Deer Lake Ave, immediately east; Wesburn Community Centre, 4781 Parkwood Ave, south of the sub-area; the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch is the Burnaby Public Library branch serving this quadrant. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Schools: SD41 (Burnaby) runs 41 elementary and 8 secondary schools city-wide, with no middle-school tier — elementary K–7, secondary 8–12. Ministry-listed schools in or beside this sub-area include Douglas Road Elementary (K–7), 4861 Canada Way, Cascade Heights Elementary (K–7), 4343 Smith Ave, at the south side, and Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway, at the east side. One completed SD41 locator run is documented: for 4861 Canada Way, Douglas Road Elementary and Burnaby Central Secondary. Every other catchment is not verified — check the exact address in the locator.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Burnaby Hospital

items.t: Hazards and campus-edge diligence: no area-wide hazard designation for this sub-area's residential streets was confirmed in the sources read; parcel-level hazard status is a property-specific check. Fraser Health's July 2025 construction notice covered paving and repainting on Kincaid Street with single-lane alternating traffic and a temporarily relocated bus stop — confirm current construction effects street by street near the campus.

ALR rules (for completeness — no ALR parcel is confirmed here): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; SPA s. 239; ALCA s. 21(1)); ALC residence caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tiered ($2,500 on 0.8–4 ha; $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha; $10,000 under 0.8 ha; applications by Oct 31) — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR. Check the parcel on ALC mapping before applying any of this.

blocks.text: Good to know about Burnaby Hospital

items.t: The zoning bylaw most older Burnaby documents cite no longer governs (2026): Zoning Bylaw 2026 No. 14815 was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, and the Burnaby 2050 OCP was adopted December 9, 2025 — a lot memo, appraisal or listing sheet still working from the 1998 OCP or the pre-2026 zoning is working from superseded paper.

The Deer Lake boardwalk by the boat launch is closed from September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive — park-edge lots east of the hospital carry that construction window, not just the view.

City Hall is effectively in this sub-area's backyard: Burnaby City Hall sits at 4949 Canada Way, just east at Deer Lake — subdivision, servicing and permit questions for a lot here are answered at that counter, and the civic precinct (not a mall — there is no enclosed mall inside the sub-area) is the area's institutional anchor alongside the hospital.

blocks.text: Duplexes and half duplexes in Burnaby Hospital
What a duplex looks like in Burnaby Hospital

items.t: The usual duplex form: Burnaby consolidated its single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District — 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of 281 m² or more within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop; multi-unit lots may be stratified, and permitted forms include single-family, duplexes, multiplexes, rowhouses and secondary suites. The duplex form class here is therefore individual duplex buildings on single lots built under the zoning of their day, plus new SSMUH product as it is built. A specific duplex is verified on its title (one lot, strata plan, or subdivided pair).

blocks.text: Sources for what’s nearby each building

items.t: The Burnaby Hospital area is the residential ground around the Burnaby Hospital campus at 3935 Kincaid Street in central Burnaby, south of Canada Way and west of Deer Lake.
"Burnaby Hospital" is a board sub-area name taken from the hospital, not a City of Burnaby community-plan name; the City publishes no street-by-street boundary for it.
Burnaby City Hall at 4949 Canada Way and Deer Lake Park at 6450 Deer Lake Avenue sit just east of the area, and Cascade Heights is the neighbourhood at its south side.
The dominant building in the area is the hospital itself: a new six-storey health care pavilion with 83 beds, mostly in single-patient rooms, opened on the campus in 2026.

blocks.text: Burnaby Hospital: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Burnaby 2050 OCP, adopted December 9, 2025, now takes precedence over the Cascade Heights plan's land use map where the two conflict, so a south-side lot's density is read in the 2050 OCP first.

Hospital construction is a live local condition, not a bylaw: Fraser Health advises that sections of some hospital corridors close temporarily overnight for construction, and its July 2025 notice put single-lane alternating traffic on Kincaid Street with the eastbound bus stop at MacDonald Avenue temporarily relocated.

blocks.text: Burnaby Hospital: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Hospital entrances changed in 2026: between 6:00 a.m. and 10:00 p.m. visitors use the West Wing Entrance or the new East and South Entrances, and bus travellers are directed to the West Wing Entrance.
After hours, between 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m., entry is through the Emergency entrance, with parking in the Emergency Parking Lot, which holds five accessible stalls available 24/7.

Deer Lake Park, 6450 Deer Lake Avenue, is the area's large park, with walking trails connecting the lake to the Burnaby Art Gallery, Shadbolt Centre for the Arts, Burnaby Village Museum and Hart House restaurant.

Part of the Deer Lake boardwalk by the boat launch is closed from September 21, 2026 for a full replacement, with completion scheduled by winter 2027 and a signed detour via Sperling Avenue and Deer Lake Drive.
Wesburn Community Centre, 4781 Parkwood Avenue in Wesburn Park south of the area, has a meeting and activity room for 100 people, a spray park, a baseball diamond and a basketball court.
The Burnaby Public Library branch for this quadrant of the city is the Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch, south-west at Metrotown; the library runs four branches, one in each quadrant.

14814, the July 3, 2026 due date and penalties, and the 2026 water and garbage charges.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant lot near Burnaby Hospital?
faq.a: No verified one — there is no standing bare-land market here. Land trades as fee-simple house lots on the established streets; no named bare-land subdivision, bare-land strata plan or presale lot offering was verified.

faq.q: What can a house lot here become under the new zoning?
faq.a: Under the R1 SSMUH district in Zoning Bylaw 2026 No. 14815: 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop — and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. Confirm the parcel's zone and the 400 m test before pricing that potential in.

faq.q: Is any of this land in the ALR?
faq.a: No ALR parcel in the sub-area is confirmed; ALR status is a parcel check through the Agricultural Land Commission, not verified lot by lot here. If a parcel were in the ALR, subdivision would need ALC approval and residences could not be stratified.

faq.q: Does the hospital redevelopment help or hurt a lot purchase?
faq.a: Both, on the record: the pavilion opened in March 2026 and the Province committed $210 million on September 21, 2026 to emergency and surgical expansion, with cancer care and an acute-care tower to follow — long-term employment support, and years of Kincaid Street construction to disclose.

faq.q: Which plan governs a south-side lot — Cascade Heights or the new OCP?
faq.a: Both are read, but the Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict; the Cascade Heights Community Plan was adopted in March 2025.

faq.q: Can I buy just one side of a duplex near Burnaby Hospital?
faq.a: Only if that side is legally separate — a strata lot in a 2-lot strata plan, or its own fee-simple lot from a subdivision. None is verified by name here; a single-lot duplex sells whole. Check the title first.

faq.q: Is there a named duplex development in this sub-area?
faq.a: None verified. The duplex evidence here is the form class under Burnaby's R1 SSMUH district.

faq.q: Can a new duplex lot here be stratified so I buy one half as a strata lot?
faq.a: Burnaby's R1 rules allow lots with two or more primary units to be stratified — that is the route; the specific lot's position is not confirmed until its zoning is read.

faq.q: What is Burnaby Hospital, and what care does it provide?
faq.a: Burnaby Hospital at 3935 Kincaid Street is a large Fraser Health community hospital providing primary and secondary acute care. Fraser Health lists 24/7 emergency care, general and internal medicine, general surgery, orthopedics, gynecology, urology, level one and two obstetrics, neonatal intensive care, tertiary palliative care, adult psychiatry and outpatient clinics among its services.

faq.q: What opened at the hospital in 2026?
faq.a: A new six-storey health care pavilion and an expanded support facilities building opened to patients on March 10, 2026. The Province states the pavilion holds 83 beds, primarily in single-patient rooms with ensuite washrooms, and that the expanded support facilities building includes a larger community emergency department adding 23 treatment spaces and a dedicated mental-health zone.

faq.q: What happens next in the redevelopment?
faq.a: The Province announced a renewed plan on September 21, 2026, with $210 million for an improved and expanded emergency department and surgical unit going ahead immediately. Expanded cancer care and a new acute-care tower are to follow, building on the March 2026 pavilion opening; the announcement gives no completion date for the tower.

faq.q: Which schools serve a hospital-area address?
faq.a: It depends on the exact address, because School District No. 41 (SD41) catchments are address-based. The SD41 schools in or beside this sub-area on the Province's list are Douglas Road Elementary (K–7) at 4861 Canada Way, Cascade Heights Elementary (K–7) at 4343 Smith Avenue, and Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12) at 6011 Deer Lake Parkway; confirm any address in the SD41 locator.

It is a GVR MLS® sub-area named for Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St — the residential streets around the hospital campus in central Burnaby, south of Canada Way and west of Deer Lake. It is not a separate City community-plan name.

faq.q: What is happening with Burnaby Hospital?
faq.a: A multi-phase redevelopment: Phase 1 delivered a new six-storey pavilion with 83 beds and an expanded support facilities building, and on September 21, 2026 the Province announced a renewed plan with $210 million for an expanded emergency department and surgical unit, with expanded cancer care and a new acute-care tower to follow.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Burnaby Hospital-area address?
faq.a: It depends on the address. SD41 schools in or beside the sub-area include Douglas Road Elementary (K–7), 4861 Canada Way, Cascade Heights Elementary (K–7) at the south side and Burnaby Central Secondary (8–12), 6011 Deer Lake Parkway, at the east side; catchments are address-based and must be checked in the SD41 locator.
